sources.excerpt:
- **Builder:** Colombo Audio Electronics
- **Catalog identity:** Pulse Driver
- **Catalog type:** Overdrive / EQ / Booster
- **Identity:** Fully analog, solid-state interpretation of the Chandler/B.K. Butler Tube Driver concept, developed without the original tube.

Pulse Driver is Colombo's no-tube interpretation of the Tube Driver family. The manufacturer and surviving Reverb documentation describe the project as heavily based on the Chandler/B.K. Butler Tube Driver and intended to preserve its characteristic response while addressing perceived limitations of the original design. [1][2]

The documented front panel has four controls and a central three-way selector:
- **Drive**
- **EQ**
- **Volume**
- **additional level/shape control**
- a 3-position supply/operating selector marked **12V**, **12-?V** on surviving imagery and documentation. [2]

Because surviving marketplace images are not sufficient to unambiguously decode every panel label, the archive keeps the exact control naming conservative rather than guessing from low-resolution photographs.

- Colombo pedals are customizable in graphic treatment. [2]
- Surviving Pulse Driver marketplace examples show more than one cosmetic state; those are treated as finish/customization evidence unless hardware changes are documented.

The defining production distinction is the solid-state/no-tube architecture. No complete numbered V1/V2 chronology was established from the checked sources.
The model is intended to use standard pedal power rather than requiring the Tube Driver's original tube arrangement. [2]

No reliable dated Colombo production revision sequence was established.

Colombo's broader construction documentation describes its pedals as handmade point-to-point, without printed circuit boards. [3]

- **Exact transistor/device:** Not publicly documented in the checked sources.

- **Exact clipping diode/device:** Not publicly documented in the checked sources.

Pulse Driver aims for the warm, harmonically rich and dynamically responsive behavior of the Tube Driver concept while retaining a conventional solid-state pedal format. Its EQ section is intended to shape the characteristic low/high balance associated with the reference circuit. [1][2]

The Colombo pedal catalog and exact-model Reverb listing provide model-specific photo trails. [2][4]

1. Colombo Audio Electronics - Pedals catalog: https://colomboaudioelectronics.it/pedals/?lang=en
2. Reverb - Colombo Audio Electronics Pulse Driver: https://reverb.com/item/56224798-colombo-audio-electronics-pulse-driver
3. Colombo Audio Electronics - Custom Pedals / workshop: https://colomboaudioelectronics.it/pedali-custom/
4. Reverb - Pulse Driver Pedal: https://reverb.com/en-nl/item/94196391-pulse-driver-pedal-colombo-s-tube-driver
